comment: Master reference for the agent editor: which models and tools each vendor offers, and what each tool does. Seed data only - harness-view lets a user add, edit and remove entries, and their edits live in .claude/state/references.json in their own repository, never here. Every entry carries  and a  so a reader can tell a documented fact from a guess; nothing in here was invented.

claude-code.label: Claude Code
claude-code.notes: Agent frontmatter takes the short alias in the model field (opus / sonnet / haiku), not a dated model id. The effort field is low / medium / high / xhigh.

models.label: Claude Opus
models.note: most capable - judgment calls, planning, review gates

models.label: Claude Sonnet
models.note: balanced - code, tests and docs against a settled spec

models.label: Claude Haiku
models.note: fast and cheap - mechanical, low-judgment work

openai-codex.label: OpenAI Codex
openai-codex.notes: Tool names and descriptions are taken directly from the Codex CLI Rust source (codex-rs/core/src/tools/...), not from prose docs, since developers.openai.com does not publish a plain tool-name table. Model ids and descriptions were extracted from the embedded JSON data on the live developers.openai.com/codex/models page (fetched as raw HTML and parsed directly - an earlier AI-summarized fetch of the same page produced the same unusual names (sol/terra/luna), which was independently confirmed against the raw JSON, so these are real, not hallucinated. Already-deprecated models seen in the same page but NOT included above (excluded per 'currently offers'): gpt-5.2 and gpt-5.3-codex (deprecated for ChatGPT sign-in), and gpt-5.1-codex-max (shown with an acknowledged-migration flag, implying it is being phased out). Permission/approval behavior for each tool is governed by Codex's sandbox + approval-mode settings (e.g. workspace-write, on-request, full-auto) rather than being a fixed per-tool property, so 'yes' above means 'requires approval under default/most sandbox modes', not 'always prompts'.

models.label: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.note: Flagship GPT-5.6 model - strongest capability for complex coding, computer use, research, and cybersecurity (most capable).

models.label: GPT-5.6 Terra
models.note: Balanced GPT-5.6 model for everyday work, performance competitive with GPT-5.5 at lower cost (balanced).

models.label: GPT-5.6 Luna
models.note: Fast, affordable GPT-5.6 model - lowest cost in the family (fast-and-cheap).

models.label: GPT-5.3 Codex Spark
models.note: Text-only research preview optimized for near-instant, real-time coding iteration; ChatGPT Pro only (fastest/experimental).

models.label: GPT-5.5
models.note: Previous-generation frontier model for complex coding, computer use, and research workflows (legacy flagship, still selectable).

models.label: GPT-5.4
models.note: Frontier model for professional work; retires from Codex with ChatGPT sign-in on 2026-08-31 - replace with gpt-5.6-terra.

models.label: GPT-5.4 Mini
models.note: Fast, efficient mini model for responsive coding tasks and subagents; also retires 2026-08-31 - replace with gpt-5.6-luna.

tools.name: shell_command

tools.name: apply_patch

tools.name: update_plan
tools.desc: Records/updates the agent's step-by-step task plan (step text + pending/in_progress/completed status) shown to the user.

tools.name: view_image

tools.name: get_context_remaining
tools.desc: Reports how many tokens remain in the current context window.

tools.name: new_context
tools.desc: Starts a new context window without resetting environment/session state.

tools.name: request_permissions
tools.desc: Asks the user to grant additional sandbox/network permissions mid-task.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.desc: Pauses the turn to ask the user a question and waits for their reply.

tools.name: tool_search
tools.desc: Searches deferred/lazily-loaded tool metadata (BM25) and exposes matching tools - the mechanism Codex uses for MCP tool discovery instead of listing every MCP tool upfront.

tools.name: request_plugin_install
tools.desc: Requests installation of a connector/plugin that exactly matches a user's explicit request.

tools.name: list_available_plugins_to_install

tools.name: web_search
tools.desc: Hosted web search tool (enabled only when web_search_mode is cached/indexed/live in config).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.desc: Creates a new sub-agent to work on a delegated task.

tools.name: send_input

tools.name: send_message
tools.desc: Sends a message to an existing sub-agent without forcing a new turn.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.desc: Sends a follow-up task to an existing (non-root) sub-agent, triggering a turn if it is idle.

tools.name: resume_agent
tools.desc: Resumes a previously paused/closed sub-agent.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.desc: Waits for one or more sub-agents to reach a final status or produce a mailbox update.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.desc: Lists currently active sub-agents.

tools.name: close_agent
tools.desc: Closes a sub-agent (and open descendants) that is no longer needed.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.desc: Interrupts a sub-agent's current turn while keeping it available for further messages.

gemini-cli.label: Google Gemini CLI
gemini-cli.notes: Tool list and exact string names come from the live main-branch source (packages/core/src/tools/tool-names.ts and .../definitions/base-declarations.ts), which is the authoritative registry (ALL_BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES). The public docs site (google-gemini.github.io/gemini-cli/docs/tools/) is STALE relative to this: it still documents a 'save_memory' memory tool and does not mention write_todos, ask_user, activate_skill, the tracker_* family, enter/exit_plan_mode, update_topic, complete_task, invoke_agent, get_internal_docs, read_mcp_resource, or list_mcp_resources. save_memory does not appear anywhere in the current ALL_BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES export, so it should be treated as removed/deprecated, not current - flagged here rather than silently reported as an active tool. Two tool names referenced only inside PLAN_MODE_TOOLS ('codebase_investigator', 'cli_help') could not be independently confirmed as full built-in tools and are deliberately omitted rather than guessed at. Models: only chat/coding-relevant text models are listed; gemini-embedding-001 (embeddings-only) and the two experimental-flag-gated Gemma models (gemma-4-31b-it, gemma-4-26b-a4b-it) exist in VALID_GEMINI_MODELS but are omitted as out of scope for a 'coding-agent' seed list. A model-resolution alias layer also exists ('auto', 'pro', 'flash', 'flash-lite') that resolves to the ids above depending on account preview access - not included as separate model entries since they are not distinct models.

zai-glm.label: Z.AI GLM Coding Plan
zai-glm.notes: Z.AI's GLM Coding Plan is consumed by pointing an existing agent harness's own API base URL/auth token at Z.AI's Anthropic-compatible endpoint (https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic) or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; per Z.AI's own marketing copy it is used this way with Claude Code, Codex, Cline, Kilo Code, OpenCode, and others. Z.AI does NOT define or expose its own agent/sub-agent tool schema - when used through Claude Code, tool calls are Claude Code's own tools (Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Grep/Glob/WebFetch/WebSearch/Task/etc., as already documented in the Anthropic tools-reference table this task said is already done); when used through Codex or Gemini CLI, that harness's own tools apply instead. That is why the 'tools' array above is empty - it is not a gap, it is the verified answer. IMPORTANT DISCREPANCY: Z.AI's own docs page for Claude Code setup (docs.z.ai/scenario-example/develop-tools/claude, fetched same date) still shows the model-mapping example as ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=GLM-4.7, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL=GLM-4.7, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL=GLM-4.5-Air, and that same page explicitly recommends NOT hardcoding the mapping so it inherits future defaults automatically. This conflicts with z.ai/subscribe and z.ai/model-api (same fetch date), which advertise GLM-5.3/GLM-5.2/GLM-5-Turbo as the current lineup and do not mention GLM-4.5-Air at all. Most likely the integration-guide page is simply out of date relative to the pricing/model pages. Flagging this rather than picking one - if the harness UI needs a single 'default Sonnet-tier' and 'default Haiku-tier' mapping, that should be re-confirmed against docs.z.ai at time of use, not taken from this file.
